name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) with Interest Subvention (MISS)
summary: A revolving credit card for farm expenses at a subsidised interest rate, so you can avoid moneylenders.

benefits.headline: Crop loans at 7% interest, effectively 4% if repaid on time
details: Short-term crop loans at 7% a year under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, with an extra 3% prompt-repayment incentive that brings the effective rate to 4%.
The loan limit under the scheme was raised from ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh in Budget 2025-26. Confirm the exact limit and subsidised portion with your bank.
Loans up to ₹2 lakh are available without collateral.
Can also be used for allied activities such as dairy and fisheries.

summary: Farmers who cultivate land: owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers.
Self Help Groups and Joint Liability Groups of farmers can also apply.
Credit limit depends on your land, crops grown and cost of cultivation.

If you already have a KCC, ask your bank about renewal or limit enhancement instead of a new card.

Land records (or tenancy/lease documents for tenant farmers)
Details of the crops you grow and their area
documents.note: Used to fix your credit limit.

steps: Visit your bank branch (cooperative, regional rural or commercial bank) or apply on the bank's website under Agri Loans.
Submit the application with identity, land and crop details.
The bank checks your records and sanctions a credit limit.
Collect your card and use it for seeds, fertilizer and other farm expenses; repay by the due date to keep the lower rate.

online.label: PM-KISAN portal (KCC can be applied for using your PM-KISAN data)

offline: Your nearest bank branch or PACS (cooperative society)
Common Service Centre (CSC) for help with the form

deadline.text: Open all year; apply whenever you need credit. Plan before the sowing season so you have funds for inputs.

caveats: RBI has issued revised KCC Directions that are due to come into effect from 1 January 2027, so bank processes may change.
